segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Hello and welcome to Real Easy English, the podcast where we have everyday conversations

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: in easy English. I'm Georgie.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And I'm Neil. Don't forget to visit our website to find a text version of this podcast so you can read along.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Hi Neil, how are things?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I'm very well, thank you Georgie. And how about you? How's your week going?

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: My week's going really well, thank you.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: And I'm excited because later I have choir practice.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Ah, choir practice.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: That means you sing with other people.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: It does.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Well, that's good because we're talking all about hobbies.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And those are the activities that we do after work or college or at the weekends.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: So, Neil, I go to choir.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Do you have any hobbies?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yes, I also have a musical hobby.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I like to play guitar.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Nice. How often do you play the guitar?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: It depends. Sometimes I play for a long time and often.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Usually if I've heard a song I like, I want to learn how to play it.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And then sometimes I don play at all for a while for weeks

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: OK so you go through phases I suppose

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yeah And how about your choir Tell me more about that

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Well so I go to choir practice weekly every Monday and at the moment we practicing for a Christmas concert

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: We did just do a concert, which was really fun, and we've got another one coming.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Right, okay. And do you really enjoy the singing? How does it make you feel?

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: I love the singing because I put my phone in my bag and I just sing with my friends and we have a really nice group of people that do choir.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: So I really enjoy it.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: So, Neil, you like playing the guitar, but maybe there's a new hobby you'd like to try.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yeah. So I've been playing guitar for many years, but I don't have any training and I can't read music.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: So I thought that maybe I should learn piano and learn properly.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Oh, that would be good. Then you can play the piano with my choir.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: OK. When do I start?

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Next Monday.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: So do you have any hobbies that aren't musical?

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Yes. I like doing some exercise. So I like running and I like doing yoga. At the moment,

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: I not running regularly I running probably monthly So once a month which is not very good I like to run more

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yeah I also run but I struggle to do it regularly

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I think if you do it twice or three times a week, it's easy to keep going.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: But once you stop, you stop for a long time.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: I completely agree.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: It's difficult to stick to a routine with running, I find.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Yeah.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: It's very easy to lose your routine.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: So, Georgie, you go to choir regularly, but you don't run regularly.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: What's this word, regularly?

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Well, regularly means that you do something often as part of a regular routine.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: So, for example, I regularly get a coffee when I come to work.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: So I get a coffee most times I come to work.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: But I don't regularly buy lunch.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: I usually bring my own lunch from home.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Saves money.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Neil, what about unusual hobbies? Do you have any unusual hobbies?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I suppose I do. I quite like making sauerkraut.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: OK, sauerkraut. What is sauerkraut?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: It a kind of food You get some cabbage and you slice it thinly and you add some salt you crush it and you leave it and after a while it changes into something new which is very good for your stomach

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: OK so why do you like making sour grout Neil

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: It's very relaxing and it takes a while for it to be right.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And I think in today's world, we do lots of things that happen very quickly.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: So it's kind of old fashioned, but satisfying.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: OK, makes sense.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: I wouldn't do it, but I'm glad you have found something you love.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Well, let's recap the language we learned during the conversation.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: We had weekly, which means every week.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yes, and monthly, every month.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: We had regularly, often.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: We also heard the word choir, a group of people who sing together.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Yes.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Thanks for listening to Real Easy English.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Continue your learning on our website where you'll find worksheets and courses for all levels.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Visit

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: bbclearningenglish.com.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Next time we'll talk about the things we do to stay healthy.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Bye for now.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Bye.
